Port
Left side facing bow. Red light at night.

Speed
Ease
Sail trim visual — sheet angle ≈ 0°
Telltales streaming = good
Both yarns flowing aft. Windward flutter = too high, leeward = too low.
Ease in gusts, trim in lulls
Gust hits: ease sheet 5-10cm. Lull: trim in to keep flow.
Luffing? Trim. Stalled? Ease.
Fluttering leading edge = under-trimmed. No power + heeling = over-trimmed.
Wind Strength12 kts — Sweet spot, hike out

Clouds

  • Cu (puffy): Fair weather.
  • Cb (tower): Storm — reef early.
  • Cirrus (wispy): Change in 12-24h.

Wind Shifts

Header = wind moves bow, slows you. Lift = frees you, faster. Track compass 3-min avg.
Sail lifted? Hold. Headed? Tack.

Tides — Colombo

SW Monsoon May-Sep: 15-25kts + swell. Best learn Nov-Mar: 8-14kts. Beira Lake flat, Negombo Lagoon shallow & safe.
Windy appMet Dept SLTide Table Colombo

EXTRA: Balance & Heeling

Heel = power + drag. 10-15° is fast, 20°+ is slow. Depower sequence: ease sheet → traveler down → vang off → reef. Move weight to windward early, not after.

Navigation & Safety

Starboard tack has right-of-way
Wind from starboard = stand-on. Port gives way.
⛵️ → ⛵️ right-of-way visual
Windward gives way to Leeward
Same tack, windward boat keeps clear.
⛵️ → ⛵️ right-of-way visual
Power gives way to Sail
Exception: overtaking, narrow channel, fishing.
⛵️ → ⛵️ right-of-way visual
N
Compass rotates on scroll. True vs Magnetic: variation ~1°W in SL. Plot: 1. Mark position 2. Draw course 3. Check depth.

Safety Gear — Checklist

Lifejacket (PFD) — wear always
VHF + phone dry bag
Flares — expiry checked
Kill cord (if power)
First aid + knife
Throwable + MOB light
Wear PFD always — 80% fatalities had none.

Communication & Signals

  • • Horn: 1 short = starboard, 2 = port, 3 = astern.
  • • VHF Mayday: "MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY, this is [boat], position [lat/long], [problem], [POB], over."
  • • Night: Red = port, Green = starboard, White = stern.

Knots & Ropes

4 essentials. Learn in hands, not just eyes.

Rabbit comes out hole, around tree, back down hole. King of knots.
  1. 1Make small loop (rabbit hole)
  2. 2Rabbit up through hole
  3. 3Around standing line (tree)
  4. 4Back down hole, pull tight
Pro tip: Dress knot = tighten strands evenly. Soak line for easier learning.

Practical Skills

01
Launching & Docking
Approach into wind/current. Fenders out early. Slow is pro — you can always abort.
02
Tacking & Jibing
Tack = bow through wind (safe). Jibe = stern through wind (dangerous — duck, control boom!).
03
Anchoring
Sand/mud bottom. 5:1 scope min (7:1 overnight). Back down at 1/3 throttle to set.
04
MOB Drill
SHOUT, THROW, MARK, TURN. Quickstop: tack immediately, circle back.
SHOUT: 'MAN OVERBOARD PORT/STBD!' Keep eyes on victim.
🌍

Advanced Seamanship

GPS, Chartplotter, AIS, Autopilot — Never trust one source. Cross-check depth, visual bearings, paper backup. AIS shows ships; not all boats have it. Autopilot steers, you navigate.
Racing vs Cruising: Racing trims every 3 sec; cruising sets and sips tea. Both need sail trim basics, but risk tolerance differs.
Pro: Log everything — wind, sail, speed. Pattern > guess.

Maintenance & Boat Care

Rigging Checks

  • • Daily: look aloft — cracked swages?
  • • Halyards: chafe at sheaves.
  • • Shrouds: tension, cotter pins.
Feel lines, don't just look.

Hull Care

  • • Wash salt after sail.
  • • Antifouling yearly — Colombo growth fast.
  • • Osmosis: blisters = yard time.

Engine Basics

  • • 5-min check: fuel, oil, coolant, belt, impeller pee.
  • • Bleed fuel if air-locked.
  • • Spare: impeller, filters, belt.
If engine fails, you still have sails.
